title: GPT‑6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
titleZh: 适合所有人的 GPT‑6 和智能 UI
author: joshuawright11
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: revolvingthrow
comments.textRawHtml:
I find the Sunday roast comparison of 5.6 vs 6 very interesting. I have no doubt most people will prefer 6, yet I am almost repulsed by all the images, so much needless whitespace, checklist and so on. Feels like I'm being condescended to and treated like a child.

Given that OpenAI is making noises about merging work with chat (a horrible idea imo), and Work is very similar to Codex... I dearly hope things like these won't have any meaningful cross-polination into the actual work tools.

Seeing that the chat is based on 6.0 and not 6.1 is disappointing. The "Visual and interactive explanations" seems genuinely useful, but 6.1 is just so much better. I wouldn't truly trust the 6.1 with the explanations, but I'd trust them a fair bit more than 6.0. I understand that compute isn't infinite, but tons of people only interact with the chat and having your "things-explainer" be as good as it can be is important when people increasingly treat AI models as the source of truth, or even use them for academic learning and whatnot.

Still, the models will improve, so the visual explainer seems pretty good as an idea / mvp.
comments.textZhHtml:
我发现 5.6 与 6 的周日烘焙比较非常有趣。我毫不怀疑大多数人会更喜欢 6，但我几乎对所有图像感到厌恶，那么多不必要的空白、清单等等。感觉我像个孩子一样受到屈尊和对待。

考虑到 OpenAI 正在发出关于将工作与聊天合并的声音（在我看来，这是一个可怕的想法），而且 Work 与 Codex 非常相似......我非常希望这样的事情不会与实际的工作工具产生任何有意义的异花授粉。

看到聊天是基于 6.0 而不是 6.1 是令人失望的。 “视觉和交互式解释”似乎确实有用，但 6.1 确实要好得多。我不会真正相信 6.1 的解释，但我比 6.0 更相信他们。我知道计算不是无限的，但很多人只与聊天互动，当人们越来越多地将人工智能模型视为真理的来源，甚至将它们用于学术学习之类的时候，让你的“事物解释器”尽可能好就很重要。

模型仍然会改进，所以视觉解释器作为一个想法/mvp似乎相当不错。

children.author: DriverDaily
children.textRawHtml:
> Feels like I'm being condescended to and treated like a child.

My most used prompt in the last week is probably "Explain this concisely and simply, like I am a child".

I spent years dumbing things down and creating visuals to support it for decision makers. I am frequently asking ChatGPT to do the same for me.

children.author: PokeyCat
children.textRawHtml:
STE is very hyped for AI but has its own smells. It's designed for aircraft maintenance manuals, not software - the two don't share the same vocabulary used to "simply" describe something. I've had a coworker try and "simplify" our documentation with Claude applying STE and the results were equally appalling to read as the Claude-ism laden docs that came before, despite the reading level metrics going down on paper.

I've taken a liking to pointing agents at the Simple English Wikipedia editorial guidelines...but so much of that is for making up for shortcomings of modern Anthropic models. Codex running 6.1-sol explains things so much more clearly that I don't feel I need to assert a style guide on its output.
children.textZhHtml:
STE 对人工智能大肆宣传，但也有自己的味道。 它是为飞机维护手册而不是软件而设计的 - 两者不共享用于“简单”描述某事物的相同词汇。 我曾有一位同事尝试用 Claude 应用 STE 来“简化”我们的文档，结果读起来与之前充满 Claude 主义的文档一样令人震惊，尽管阅读水平指标已经写在纸上。

我喜欢在简单英语维基百科编辑指南中指向代理……但其中很大一部分是为了弥补现代人择模型的缺点。 运行 6.1-sol 的 Codex 解释得更加清楚，我觉得不需要在其输出上断言样式指南。

children.textZhHtml:
Gemini 3.8 对我来说总是以任何计算机科学硕士毕业生都能理解的简洁方式输出。明确，切中要点，在真正需要时提供一些背景公式，而不是散文等中的相同公式。

GPT 在文本中保留太多，恕我直言。

children.author: criley2
children.textRawHtml:
In my experience

- Gemini 3.8 has a beautiful answer. Typography, use of lists, brevity, style, even the font choice on the web harness -- all of it is A tier or even S tier. Notice I didn't say answer quality. The answer is always extremely mid, and the harder the question (or more effort needed to answer it), Google just quits. I give it a "C" on answer quality

- ChatGPT (Chat, pre 6, I assume 5.6 although they commonly hide the model picker): Ugly answer. Runs on printing page after page of unnecessary side notes. Mostly just walls of texts in paragraphs with little thought to information design. However, inside of that mess of text is almost always the answer I'm looking for, and it's almost always incredibly better than the truncated, desgined Gemini answer.

For a while I ran all of my question queries on Gemini and ChatGPT, but I noticed that I basically always picked ChatGPT's answer head to head.
children.textZhHtml:
根据我的经验

- Gemini 3.8 给出了一个漂亮的答案。版式、列表的使用、简洁性、风格，甚至网络线束上的字体选择——所有这些都是 A 层甚至 S 层。请注意，我没有说答案质量。答案总是非常中间，问题越难（或者需要更多的努力来回答它），谷歌就会退出。我在答案质量上给它一个“C”

-ChatGPT（Chat，pre 6，我假设 5.6，尽管它们通常隐藏模型选择器）：丑陋的答案。逐页打印不必要的旁注。大部分只是段落中的文字墙，很少考虑信息设计。然而，在那堆混乱的文本中几乎总是我正在寻找的答案，而且它几乎总是比截断的、设计的 Gemini 答案好得多。

有一段时间，我在 Gemini 和 ChatGPT 上运行了所有问题查询，但我注意到我基本上总是直接选择 ChatGPT 的答案。

children.author: spockz
children.textRawHtml:
Interesting that this hasn’t been my experience. ChatGPT has often gave me with pages of text dripping with confidence about a solution for my problem. Diving very quickly into implementation details. Even if I tell it to stay in the problem and product fit level. Gemini on the other hand somehow always outputs at the level that I am expecting and reasoning.

I even found it was capable of stepping back from code implementation and bug hunting to “hang on, it’s not the algorithm that is incorrectly implemented, it is the wrong algorithm for the goal.” GPT Sol (5.6,6 and 6.1) just kept hammering in the problem.
children.textZhHtml:
有趣的是，这并不是我的经历。 ChatGPT 经常给我提供几页文字，充满信心地告诉我问题的解决方案。快速深入了解实施细节。即使我告诉它留在问题和产品适合的水平。 另一方面，Gemini 总是以我期望和推理的水平输出。

我什至发现它能够从代码实现和 bug 寻找中退一步，“坚持下去，这不是算法实现不正确，而是算法实现了错误的目标。” GPT Sol（5.6、6 和 6.1）一直在解决这个问题。

children.author: BoxOfRain
children.textRawHtml:
The problem with Claudish isn't that it's technically poor English, the problem is that it's information-sparse waffle most of the time. It's like dealing with a colleague who needs several paragraphs of tedious preamble to make a point when you just want them to spit it out and be done with it. It also does a great deal of vague gesturing at thoughts without actually instantiating them directly, for example by using the same tired metaphors to the point they don't actually convey a thought any more.

If I say Claude talks like a meringue it's patently obvious what I'm trying to convey, sweet but full of empty space. If you hear that same metaphor day-in day-out then after a while it doesn't call up a thought at all, it's just an annoying verbal habit.
children.textZhHtml:
Claudish 的问题不在于它的英语技术很差，问题在于它大多数时候都是信息稀疏的华夫饼。这就像与一位需要几段乏味的序言来阐明观点的同事打交道，而你只想让他们把它说出来并完成它。它还对想法进行了大量模糊的手势，而不实际直接实例化它们，例如，通过使用相同的疲倦的隐喻，以至于它们实际上不再传达想法。

如果我说克劳德像蛋白酥皮一样说话，那显然是我想要传达的东西，甜蜜但充满了空虚的空间。如果你日复一日地听到同样的比喻，那么过了一段时间它就不再引起你的思考了，这只是一种令人讨厌的语言习惯。
